reason: The invoice bug last month is exactly this problem and I like that the comparison is plain code, but I can't just drop an unknown open source tool that records our app and calls Meta's API into our workflow. It would need to get through security review first, and I'm not spending my week writing that justification for a project I've never heard of.
objection: Who maintains this and will it still exist in six months? Recordings of our app in use will contain real customer data, and the fact that one path sends data to Meta is enough for security to say no before they read the rest.
would_change_my_mind: A fully offline mode with the AI parts switched off by default, plus proof it caught a real regression on a codebase like ours, so I can show my manager a concrete case instead of a README demo.
